lesson_title: Turning a Story into a Sum
hook_text: Bread R18, milk R24, pay with R50. Do not grab a calculator yet. Write the story first.
clip_script: Spaza shop in Soweto. Bread R18, milk R24, you hand over R50. Do not work anything out yet. Write the story as a sentence. Two things bought together: 18 plus 24. Taken from fifty: 50 minus, open bracket, 18 plus 24, close bracket, equals box. The brackets say add first. The box is the change you do not know yet. Now check: read it back. Fifty rand, take away the bread and milk together, leaves the change. That is the story. Estimate: about R40 spent, so about R10 change. Now the trap. Lerato has 27 marbles, Sipho has 19, how many more does Lerato have? More sounds like plus. It is not. Two piles side by side, measure the gap: 27 minus 19 equals box. Words hint, the story decides. Sentence first, answer second.
visual_style: Whiteboard till receipt turning into a number sentence sign by sign; two piles of marbles with a gap measured between them.
mood: Calm detective, reading the clues before acting.
pacing: One two-step story built sign by sign, the read-back check, then the one trap and the rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write a number sentence for the next thing you buy.
